summary: Validated update (valid; effect: interpretation append for the recovery-authority question, rationale only). It re-verifies that account's central mechanism directly in the captured source rather than from memory: the only places that call makeBallot and broadcast a fresh Prepare from inside a proposal phase sit within `if r.IsLeader` blocks - epaxos/epaxos.go:855-868 in handlePreAcceptReply and 1016-1033 in handleAcceptReply - and both are reached only after the nacks exceed half the configuration. That is exactly what the account asserts, so with IsLeader false at a plain recovering replica the periodic retry repeats the same rejected ballot and no repair is enabled; nothing else about the account changed. Run state at this point: six questions with explained dispositions and controller receipts - value adoption replacing the quorum-reported command with a NOOP up to a completed contradiction of a live replica's committed value, bounded to coordinators that lack the command by an executed control run (Q1); recovery authority bounded by the recoverer's fixed ballot with the restart path gated on IsLeader, now source-verified (Q2); the status-guard stall that clears only on the executor's retry (Q3); the client-completion contract holding for the single-NOOP case through re-propose but not for the empty batch (Q4); the wrong-row write in handlePreAccept refuted as unreachable (Q5); and the equal-ballot empty-slice replacement decided by the reply adopted at the slow-quorum trigger position, measured over all six permutations of the three-reply set and four orders of a two-carrier/two-empty set, final because only N - SlowQuorumSize replies can follow (Q6). Eleven receipts, seven registered source materials spanning the recovery, executor and decoder paths, both facts and all behaviour entries consistent in statements, conditions, dependency pointers and citations, and the captured snapshot untouched.
